editable_controls.name: Hall Reverb2
editable_controls.description: Controls the amount of time it takes for the reverberation to decay away to a very low level after the input signal stops. editable_controls.name: HF DAMPING
editable_controls.description: This parameter controls the rate of attenuation of high frequencies in the decay of the reverberation. editable_controls.name: ENV LEV (1 to 9)
editable_controls.description: These parameters control the output tap levels sequenced in time across the density from input to output. Envelope Level 1 is tapped right after the diffusers and before the echoes (see the diagram). If this is undesirable, set ENV LEV1 to 0. Envelope Levels 8 and 9 are positioned at the very end of the Density; setting these too high can cause excessive ringing. Envelope Levels 8 and 9 are also very dry. Set all nine tap levels to find the envelope for your application. We recommend the average Envelope Level not to exceed a value of 45 to prevent overdriving these reverbs
editable_controls.evidence: ASR-10 Musician's Manual; not independently verified in the OS emulator

editable_controls.name: HF DAMPING
editable_controls.description: This parameter controls the rate of attenuation of high frequencies in the decay of the reverberation. As natural reverb decays, some high frequencies tend to get absorbed by the environment. Increasing the value of this parameter will gradually filter out (dampen) more and more high frequency energy
editable_controls.evidence: ASR-10 Musician's Manual; not independently verified in the OS emulator

editable_controls.name: HF BANDWIDTH
editable_controls.description: The high frequency bandwidth acts as a low pass filter on the signal going into the reverb, controlling the amount of high frequencies that will pass into the effect. The higher the setting, the more high frequencies are allowed to pass. This functions like a tone control on a guitar
editable_controls.evidence: ASR-10 Musician's Manual; not independently verified in the OS emulator

editable_controls.name: DIFFUS1
editable_controls.description: This parameter smears the input signal transients, to diffuse and smooth the sound. Lower values will cause impulse sounds to appear as a series of discrete echoes, while higher values tend to increase the smear (smoother sounding with fewer discrete echoes). We recommend settings of 50 for starters
editable_controls.evidence: ASR-10 Musician's Manual; not independently verified in the OS emulator

editable_controls.name: DIFFUS2
editable_controls.description: This parameter, similar to and in series with Room Diffusion1, performs the same way but controls lower frequency ranges. Experiment with different levels between the diffuser parameters to find the settings that are right for your source
editable_controls.evidence: ASR-10 Musician's Manual; not independently verified in the OS emulator

editable_controls.description: Density 1 controls the number of echoes

editable_controls.name: DENSTY 2
editable_controls.description: Density 2 controls the number of echoes in a lower frequency range. In general to get the smoothest sound, DENSTY 2 is usually less than the value of DENSTY 1
